identity_rationale: Erving Goffman, identified by The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (Anchor US edition) and Asylums. Existing curated person ID reused; no new authority ID or namesake merger.

screening.role: Selection context only, not substantive proof or automatic identity resolution.

sources.title: Erving Goffman, The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life: introduction excerpt, MIT-hosted scan
sources.note: Title page and introduction printed pp. 1–5 (PDF pp. 2–4) read via OCR. Doubleday Anchor witness; incomplete excerpt without a consulted copyright page. Remaining introduction and complete book unread; claims use read text, while edition dates use separate publisher metadata.

sources.note: Institutional archive’s indexed heading identifies Goffman as 1922–1982 and ASA president. Full page denied access during this check; only indexed institutional identity/life years are asserted, not a new full-biography reading.

substantive_relations.relationship: Studies situated encounters through participants’ attempts to establish and manage a definition of the situation.
substantive_relations.note: Own introduction pp. 1–4 read; social inference and interactional responses are the object, not evidence that he founded practice-oriented historiography.

substantive_relations.relationship: Distinguishes intentionally given expressions from impressions others infer from expressions given off.
substantive_relations.note: Own introduction pp. 1–5 read. A specific resource for examining socially performed identities; not a claim of direct influence on all identity histories or an equation of tactical self-presentation with all diasporic identity formation.

limits: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. Source notes state actual reading extent; no complete monograph or comprehensive reception survey is claimed. Existing collective relationships and source/roster qualifications remain.
